anzsic_codes.name: Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
Salesforce, Inc. (**Salesforce**), through its wholly owned subsidiary, proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Intercom, Inc. (**Intercom**).

Salesforce is a global supplier of customer relationship management (**CRM**) software and other software-as-a-service solutions that enable companies to manage and improve their relationships with customers. Salesforce’s core offerings are CRM solutions designed for the sales, service, marketing and commerce functions within a company. Salesforce also offers the following products:

* Agentforce Service (formerly Service Cloud), a CRM solution for service functions which offers a set of tools, including case management, omnichannel support, workflow automation and analytics, for both external customer use cases and internal stakeholder use cases. Agentforce Service is designed to work with Salesforce’s broader CRM environment.
* Agentforce Service Agent and Agentforce Help Agent, AI agent solutions that have been built to support the Agentforce Service suite of offerings. These products are autonomous AI agents for conversational customer service that can understand and respond to customer inquiries without human intervention.
* Qualified’s ‘Piper’, an inbound AI-based sales development representative agent solution designed to engage and convert inbound buyers.

Intercom (recently rebranded as Fin) is a global provider of customer service software. Its core products include:

* Intercom Helpdesk, a customer service management solution used by human customer support agents. Its features including an omnichannel inbox, AI-enhanced ticketing, knowledge management, proactive customer engagement tools, and reporting and analytics.
* Fin, an agentic AI product for customer service that typically works on top of Intercom’s Helpdesk or another provider’s helpdesk solution.

events.title: Salesforce - Intercom - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Salesforce, Inc. (Salesforce), through its wholly owned subsidiary,
proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Intercom, Inc. (Intercom)
(the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Salesforce, is a global supplier of customer
relationship management (CRM) software and other software-as-a-
service solutions. Salesforce’s CRM platform assists users with
sales, service, marketing and commerce functions.
Relevant to the assessment of this Acquisition, Salesforce also
offers the following products:
• Agentforce Service (formerly Service Cloud), a CRM solution
for service functions which offers a set of tools, including
case management, omnichannel support, workflow
automation and analytics, for both external customer use
cases and internal stakeholder use cases. Agentforce
Service is designed to work with Salesforce’s broader CRM
environment.
• Agentforce Service Agent and Agentforce Help Agent, AI
agent solutions that have been built to support the
Agentforce Service suite of offerings. These products are
autonomous AI agents for conversational customer service
that can understand and respond to customer inquiries
without human intervention.
• Qualified’s ‘Piper’, an inbound AI-based sales development
representative agent solution designed to engage and
convert inbound buyers.
The target, Intercom (recently rebranded as Fin), is also a global
provider of CRM software. Its core products include:
• Intercom Helpdesk, a customer service management
solution used by human customer support agents. Its
features including an omnichannel inbox, AI-enhanced
ticketing, knowledge management, proactive customer
engagement tools, and reporting and analytics.
• Fin, an agentic AI product for customer service that typically
works on top of Intercom’s Helpdesk or another provider’s
helpdesk solution.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
Salesforce and Intercom (together, the Parties) overlap in the supply
of CRM solutions. In particular, the Parties both offer CRM products
that provide customer service, agentic AI customer service, and
agentic AI marketing/sales agent functionality.
There is also a non-horizontal relationship, with Intercom’s products
(including Fin and Helpdesk) able to be integrated with Salesforce's
CRM software via API.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The aggregation in the supply of CRM software in Australia as a
result of the Acquisition is estimated to be low.
• Salesforce and Intercom are not close competitors given
differences in their customer bases. In particular, Salesforce’s
software is directed at large enterprises while Intercom’s
offerings are designed for small and medium enterprise
businesses.
• Post-Acquisition, Salesforce is unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rivals’ access to CRM services given the
availability of alternative suppliers of CRM services.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
